text:
Before you hire someone to get you found on Google, Google them.

Type "SEO" and their suburb into your phone.

If they can't get their own business showing up in their own backyard, I'd be asking how they plan to do it for yours.

Google Ads changes all the time.

September 1: lots of Search campaigns moved to AI Max.
October 12: Google started pulling offers off websites into ads.

You run a business. You shouldn't have to keep up with that.

Keeping up is my job.

A client's ads were bringing back about four dollars for every one they put in.

They asked how to double their leads.

My head went straight to new audiences, new angles, new creative.

The answer was simpler.

Increase the budget. When the machine works, feed it.

I got my own business ranking on Google in my local area.

No tricks. The same steady work I do for clients:

A Google Business Profile kept current.
A website that answers what people search.
Showing up month after month.

Heavy lifting up front. Then it builds.

You don't read your mechanic's service bulletins. You just want the ute to start.

Google Ads is the same. New settings land every few weeks, and some switch themselves on.

Someone should be checking your account every week.

Who's checking yours?

You own a fishing shop. You pay someone to hand out flyers at the Hillarys boat ramp.

One day they start handing them out at the footy too. Without asking.

Plenty more flyers gone. Hardly any more customers.

That's AI Max in your Google Ads when nobody's watching.
